spots.why: The symbol of Paris: 330 m of wrought iron built for the 1889 World Fair. Views from the 2nd floor are often better than from the summit.
spots.shot: Both of you under the tower looking up, or the full tower from the Trocadéro esplanade.
spots.tips: Book the summit early on toureiffel.paris (summit tickets sell out). Sparkles for 5 min on the hour after dark, last one at 23:00.
spots.dec: Dark by about 17:00 in December, so a late-afternoon slot gives daylight going up and the lights coming down.
spots.price: Summit by lift €36.70 · stairs+lift €28 · 2nd floor lift €23.50 · stairs €14.80 (2026 adult)
spots.go: Bir-Hakeim (M6) · Champ de Mars–Tour Eiffel (RER C)

spots.why: Napoleon's triumphal arch over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, with 12 avenues radiating from the Étoile. The roof gives the best view down the Champs-Élysées.
spots.shot: Under the arch by the eternal flame, or the Champs-Élysées lights seen from the roof.
spots.tips: Reach it through the underground passage; never cross the roundabout. About 284 steps to the roof. The flame is rekindled every evening at 18:30.
spots.dec: At dusk the roof overlooks the Christmas lights on the Champs-Élysées (from 22 Nov 2026).
spots.free: Under 18 and EEA residents under 26; everyone on the 1st Sunday, Nov–Mar
spots.go: Charles de Gaulle–Étoile (M1, M2, M6, RER A)

spots.why: The 1.9 km avenue from Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe: parades, flagship stores and Paris's best-known Christmas lights.
spots.shot: The lit avenue looking up to the Arc de Triomphe.
spots.tips: Walk it downhill from the Arc at dusk.
spots.dec: 2026 lights from 22 Nov (lit 17:00–01:00, all night on 24 and 31 Dec). The Christmas market is back after about 10 years: 22 Nov 2026–4 Jan 2027.
spots.go: George V (M1) · Franklin D. Roosevelt (M1, M9)

spots.n: Place de la Concorde & Luxor Obelisk
spots.nf: Place de la Concorde et obélisque de Louxor
spots.why: Paris's largest square, where Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were guillotined, with a 3,300-year-old Egyptian obelisk and views to the Arc, the Madeleine and the Assemblée.
spots.shot: The gilded obelisk tip with the Eiffel Tower behind it.

spots.why: Paris's most ornate bridge (1900), with gilded winged horses, Art Nouveau lamps and the Invalides dome at one end and the Grand Palais at the other.
spots.shot: The two of you at a lamp post with the Eiffel Tower in the background.
spots.tips: Magical when the lamps come on at dusk.

spots.nf: Pont Neuf et square du Vert-Galant
spots.why: Paris's oldest standing bridge (completed 1607), joining the tip of the Île de la Cité, where the little Vert-Galant garden points down the Seine like a ship's prow.
spots.shot: The willow at the tip of the island with the Seine around it.

spots.why: The iron footbridge between the Louvre and the Institut de France, with a classic view of the Île de la Cité. The love locks were removed in 2015; please do not add any.
spots.shot: The Île de la Cité and Pont Neuf at sunset.

spots.why: Paris's most elegant square: the Austerlitz column, the Ritz and the great jewellers (Boucheron, Chaumet, Van Cleef & Arpels, Dior Joaillerie; Cartier is round the corner on Rue de la Paix).
spots.shot: The column framed by the lit fir trees.
spots.dec: Christmas 2026 (from 17 Nov): eight 10 m fir trees round the column, light arches in the nearby streets, and lit jewellers' fronts. One of the most beautiful Christmas sights in Paris.

spots.why: Paris's oldest planned square (1612): red-brick arcades round a garden, with Victor Hugo's house at no. 6.
spots.shot: The arcades with the fountain garden behind.
spots.tips: Combine with the Marais, Carette (tea room under the arcades) and the Maison de Victor Hugo (free).

spots.nf: Jardin du Palais-Royal et colonnes de Buren
spots.why: Arcaded gardens next to the Louvre, with Daniel Buren's striped columns ('Les Deux Plateaux', 1986) in the main courtyard.
The neoclassical temple where France buries its great people (Voltaire, Rousseau, Hugo, Marie Curie, Josephine Baker), with Foucault's pendulum under the dome.
spots.tips: The dome's outdoor colonnade is usually open only in the warmer months (check).
spots.free: EEA residents under 26; everyone on the 1st Sunday, Nov–Mar

spots.nf: Les Invalides et tombeau de Napoléon
spots.why: Louis XIV's veterans' hospital: Napoleon's red porphyry tomb under the golden dome, and the Musée de l'Armée, one of the world's great military museums.
spots.shot: The golden dome from the esplanade, or the tomb seen from the balustrade.

ph.by: Another one of my pictures: This photograph was taken by Medium69 (William Cr…

spots.why: A medieval royal palace that became the Revolution's prison: the vast Gothic Hall of the Men-at-Arms and Marie-Antoinette's chapel.
spots.shot: The vaulted Hall of the Men-at-Arms.
spots.tips: Combined ticket with the Sainte-Chapelle next door.

spots.why: The 1875 opera house that inspired The Phantom of the Opera: the grand staircase, the gilded Grand Foyer and Chagall's 1964 ceiling.
spots.tips: The auditorium is often closed for rehearsals, so check the day before. Pair it with the Galeries Lafayette and Printemps windows next door.
spots.dec: Five minutes from the Christmas windows on Boulevard Haussmann.

spots.why: The 1900 glass-and-steel nave, fully reopened in 2025 after restoration. It hosts the big exhibitions, including the Centre Pompidou's while that is closed.
spots.dec: "Grand Palais des Glaces": an ice rink under the nave with a 16 m moon, about 12 Dec 2026–6 Jan 2027 (€27–39). Exhibitions: "Girls" (from 9 Dec), "Cézanne et nous".

spots.why: Paris's neo-Renaissance city hall, rebuilt after 1871, with free exhibitions inside.
The red windmill of the 1889 cabaret that made the French cancan famous. The façade alone is worth a photo; for the show, see Night out.
Old quarry tunnels holding the remains of about 6 million Parisians, stacked into walls of skulls and bones. Reopened on 8 April 2026 with a renovated route.
spots.shot: A wall of skulls and bones (no flash).
spots.tips: Many steps down and back up; the tunnels stay at about 14 °C all year. Not for the claustrophobic.

spots.n: Statue of Liberty replica (Île aux Cygnes)
spots.nf: Statue de la Liberté (île aux Cygnes)
spots.why: The quarter-scale bronze replica at the tip of the Île aux Cygnes, at the end of a peaceful tree-lined walk from Bir-Hakeim.
spots.shot: The statue with the Seine behind.

spots.why: Europe's biggest business district, at the far end of the historic axis that runs from the Louvre through the Arc de Triomphe.
spots.dec: Île-de-France's biggest Christmas market, with 300+ chalets and an ice rink: 12 Nov–31 Dec 2026 (some sources say 3 Jan).

spots.why: Louis XIV's palace and the model for every European court: the Hall of Mirrors, the royal apartments, the gardens, the Trianons and Marie-Antoinette's hamlet.
spots.shot: Both of you in the Hall of Mirrors.
spots.tips: Arrive at opening and see the palace first, then the gardens. Closed on Mondays. In winter the gardens are free and the fountains are off. In town, L'Épi du Roi bakery won best croissant in France in 2026.
spots.dec: "Le Parcours du Roi" (12 Dec 2026–2 Jan 2027): an evening show-visit on Marie-Antoinette with Père Noël at the end. Christmas concerts in the Royal Chapel on 5, 11, 12–13 and 19 Dec. Free on Sun 6 Dec (timed slot).
spots.free: Under 18 and EEA residents under 26; 1st Sunday Nov–Mar
spots.go: Versailles Château Rive Gauche (RER C, ~40 min)

spots.why: Part of Versailles: the pink-marble Grand Trianon, the Petit Trianon and the Queen's thatched hamlet, a short walk from the crowds.
spots.shot: The Queen's Hamlet across the pond.
spots.tips: Included in the Passport ticket. Opens at noon (check winter hours).
spots.go: Versailles Château Rive Gauche (RER C) + 25 min walk or the little train

spots.why: Home to French kings for eight centuries (UNESCO), from François I's Renaissance gallery to the horseshoe staircase where Napoleon said farewell in 1814. Calmer than Versailles.
spots.shot: The horseshoe staircase in the Cour des Adieux.
spots.go: Fontainebleau-Avon (Transilien R from Gare de Lyon, ~40 min) + bus 1

spots.why: The château whose splendour made Louis XIV jealous enough to jail its owner, Fouquet, and then hire the same architects to build Versailles. Its Christmas is one of the best in France.
spots.shot: The château lit up at night across the garden.
spots.dec: "Le Grand Noël" 2026, 14 Nov–3 Jan: the château decorated as 9 stops around the world, a monumental projection and an ice rink (€5). Open into the evening. Closed 25 Dec and 1 Jan, and on Mondays and Tuesdays outside school holidays.
spots.price: €25.90 weekdays / €27.90 weekends & holidays (Grand Noël 2026); shuttle packages from Paris ~€50.90
spots.go: Melun (RER D / Transilien R, ~30 min) + shuttle or taxi

spots.nf: Château de Chantilly et Grandes Écuries
spots.why: A fairy-tale château on a lake: the Musée Condé (France's largest collection of old paintings after the Louvre), Le Nôtre's gardens and the 18th-century Great Stables. Home of crème Chantilly.
spots.shot: The château reflected in its moat.
spots.dec: Equestrian Christmas show "Le Noël oublié" under the Great Stables dome, 28 Nov 2026–3 Jan 2027.
spots.go: Chantilly-Gouvieux (TER from Gare du Nord, ~25 min) + 20 min walk

spots.why: The tallest medieval keep in Europe (52 m) and a Sainte-Chapelle of its own, at the end of metro line 1.
spots.shot: The keep from the inner courtyard.

spots.why: Louis XIV's birthplace, now France's national archaeology museum, with Le Nôtre's long terrace looking over Paris.
spots.shot: The skyline of La Défense from the terrace.

spots.why: Napoleon and Joséphine's country house, kept with its Empire interiors.
The greatest Loire château: François I's Renaissance fantasy with a double-helix staircase often credited to Leonardo da Vinci. A long day trip; a tour is easiest.
spots.shot: The double-helix staircase or the rooftop forest of chimneys.
spots.dec: Christmas decorations and trees in December (check dates).
spots.go: Blois (train from Paris-Austerlitz, ~1h30) + shuttle or tour

ph.by: No machine-readable author provided. Calips assumed (based on copyright claims).

spots.why: The 'ladies' château' arching over the River Cher, famous for its flower arrangements and, in December, its Christmas decorations.
spots.dec: "Noël à Chenonceau": the château decorated for the season (check dates).
spots.go: Chenonceaux station via Tours (~2h30) or a Loire tour

spots.why: The world's most visited museum (about 9 million visitors in 2025): the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, the Winged Victory and 35,000 works in a former royal palace.
spots.shot: Both of you with the glass pyramid at dusk, or the Winged Victory on the Daru staircase.
spots.tips: Book a timed slot. Enter through the Carrousel or Porte des Lions to skip the pyramid queue. Pick 3–4 wings rather than trying to see it all. Closed on Tuesdays. The Apollo Gallery reopened in July 2026 without the jewels after the October 2025 robbery; check that it is open.
spots.dec: Free on the 1st Friday evening of the month: Fri 4 Dec 2026. Exhibitions: Kader Attia & Elizabeth Peyton (until 14 Dec), "Le trésor du Louvre" (until 19 Dec).
spots.free: Under 18 and EEA residents under 26; 1st Friday evening (not Jul–Aug)

spots.why: The world's greatest Impressionist collection (Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Degas, Manet) in a Beaux-Arts railway station of 1900.
spots.shot: The giant clock window looking across the Seine towards the Louvre (5th floor).
spots.tips: Thursday late opening until 21:45. Closed on Mondays. Go straight to the 5th-floor Impressionist galleries.
spots.dec: "Mary Cassatt" exhibition until 31 Jan 2027.
spots.price: €16 online / €14 at the desk; Thursday evening €12
spots.free: Under 18 and EEA residents under 26; 1st Sunday (booking)

spots.why: Monet's Water Lilies, eight huge panels in two oval rooms designed with him, plus the Walter-Guillaume collection.
Rodin's mansion and rose garden, home to The Thinker, The Kiss and The Gates of Hell.
spots.shot: The Thinker in the garden with the Invalides dome behind.

spots.n: Musée du quai Branly – Jacques Chirac
spots.why: Arts of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas in Jean Nouvel's building behind a living plant wall, next to the Eiffel Tower.
spots.shot: The vertical garden wall on the quai.

ph.by: Another one of my pictures: This photograph was taken by Medium69 (William Cr…

spots.why: Europe's largest modern-art museum, CLOSED from 22 Sep 2025 until 2030 for renovation. Its exhibitions are at the Grand Palais in the meantime. The Stravinsky Fountain outside is still worth a look.
spots.shot: The inside-out façade from the piazza.

spots.why: The world's largest Picasso collection, in a 17th-century Marais mansion.
spots.shot: The grand staircase of the Hôtel Salé.

spots.why: The free museum of Paris history, from prehistoric canoes to Proust's bedroom, in two Marais mansions.
The free city fine-arts museum in a 1900 palace, with a hidden garden café under a mosaic colonnade.
spots.shot: The semicircular garden and its colonnade.

spots.n: Musée de Cluny – Museum of the Middle Ages
spots.nf: Musée de Cluny – musée du Moyen Âge
spots.why: The Lady and the Unicorn tapestries and Roman baths under a Gothic abbots' mansion.
spots.shot: The Lady and the Unicorn room.

spots.why: The world's largest Monet collection, including 'Impression, Sunrise', the painting that named Impressionism.
A Second Empire mansion of art collectors (Italian Renaissance, Rembrandt, Fragonard), reopened in 2024, with one of Paris's prettiest tea rooms.
Frank Gehry's glass-sailed building in the Bois de Boulogne, with major modern-art exhibitions.
spots.shot: The glass 'sails' from the water terrace.
spots.dec: Exhibition around the collector Gustave Fayet (Van Gogh, Gauguin, Redon) in Dec 2026.
spots.go: Les Sablons (M1) + 10 min walk, or the shuttle from Étoile

spots.why: Tadao Ando's concrete cylinder inside an 18th-century round grain exchange, showing François Pinault's contemporary art.
spots.shot: The domed rotunda from the top walkway.

spots.why: The contemporary-art foundation's new home since autumn 2025, in a Haussmann building opposite the Louvre redesigned by Jean Nouvel.
French decorative arts and fashion over 800 years, in a wing of the Louvre palace.
The Dior museum at 30 Montaigne: the spiral staircase of miniature dresses and the original salons. Tickets go weeks ahead.
spots.shot: The rainbow staircase of 452 miniature dresses.
spots.dec: Pair it with the 2026 Dior Christmas façade and windows at 30 Montaigne.

spots.why: Saint Laurent's couture house, kept as it was, with his studio.
The 18th-century royal furniture store on Place de la Concorde, restored in 2021: gilded apartments and a loggia over the square.
spots.shot: The loggia over Place de la Concorde.

spots.why: The natural-history museum's spectacular hall, with a parade of stuffed animals under a glass roof, in the Jardin des Plantes.
spots.shot: The animal parade from the top balcony.

spots.why: Immersive digital-art shows projected over the walls and floor of an old foundry.
Free city collection of 20th-century art, including Dufy's enormous 'La Fée Électricité'.
Victor Hugo's apartment on the Place des Vosges, with his Chinese drawing room. Free.
Renoir's old studio and gardens, overlooking Montmartre's vineyard.
spots.shot: The Renoir gardens and the swing.

spots.why: Paris's wax museum (1882), with a Belle Époque Palace of Mirages.
A private collection of working antique fairground rides in Bercy wine warehouses; visits by booking only. Usually holds a winter "Festival du Merveilleux" at the end of December (check).

spots.n: Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace
spots.why: One of the oldest aviation museums in the world, with two Concordes and an Ariane rocket.
spots.go: Le Bourget (RER B) + bus, or M7 La Courneuve + bus

spots.why: The Gothic masterpiece, reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire, brighter than in centuries. About 11 million visitors in its first year back.
spots.shot: The west façade from the parvis, or the rose window inside.
spots.tips: Entry is free. Book the optional free timed slot on notredamedeparis.fr (released about 2 days ahead) or queue. Late opening on Thursdays until 22:00. Beware of fake paid tickets.
spots.dec: Christmas 2026 at the cathedral: masses on 24 Dec at 16:00, 18:00 and 20:00, vigil at 23:00 and midnight mass; on 25 Dec at 8:30, 10:00 and 11:30. Free, no booking; arrive 30 min early. Christmas market in Square René-Viviani, 26 Nov–27 Dec.

spots.why: The climb up the north tower to the gargoyles and the great bells, with a view over the new spire and the Seine.
spots.tips: About 420 steps, no lift. Booking a slot is required.

spots.why: Louis IX's 1248 chapel built for the Crown of Thorns: 15 stained-glass windows, more glass than wall. Breathtaking on a sunny day.
spots.tips: Go on a sunny morning. It is inside the courthouse, so expect a security queue.
spots.dec: Christmas concerts 18–29 Dec 2026 (Vivaldi's Four Seasons, Messiah on 19–20 Dec, carols on 24 and 26 Dec), about €20–60.
spots.price: €16 EEA / €22 non-EEA (2026); combined with the Conciergerie €23/€30

spots.why: The white basilica on top of Montmartre (completed in 1914), with a panoramic view over Paris from its steps and dome.
spots.shot: The view of Paris from the front steps.
spots.tips: The basilica is free. The dome (€8, about 280 steps) has the 2nd-highest view in Paris. Watch for the "string bracelet" scam on the steps. The funicular takes a metro ticket.

spots.why: Paris's second-largest church: Delacroix murals, a famous organ and the brass meridian line from The Da Vinci Code.
A soaring Gothic-Renaissance church by Les Halles, home to one of France's largest organs (free Sunday recitals).
spots.go: Les Halles (M4, RER A, B, D)

spots.why: A church built as a Greek temple to Napoleon's army, surrounded by gourmet shops. Frequent classical and Christmas concerts.
Paris's oldest church (its bell tower dates from about 1000), with a painted interior restored in 2020.
The only surviving rood screen in Paris, the shrine of Saint Geneviève, and the steps from 'Midnight in Paris' outside.
The 1926 Hispano-Moorish mosque with a calm green-tiled courtyard and garden. Its tea room serves mint tea and pastries.
The birthplace of Gothic architecture and the burial place of almost every French king and queen, Marie-Antoinette included. Underrated.
spots.shot: The royal tombs in the crypt.

spots.why: The world's most visited cemetery: a hillside of tombs and trees with Chopin, Oscar Wilde, Édith Piaf and Jim Morrison.
spots.tips: Download a map; it is huge and hilly. Closes around 17:30 in winter.

ph.by: Connie Ma from Chicago, United States of America

spots.why: A peaceful cemetery below a road bridge, with Degas, Stendhal, Dalida and Truffaut.
The best-preserved High Gothic cathedral (UNESCO), with 12th–13th-century stained glass in "Chartres blue" and a labyrinth set in the floor.
spots.shot: The rose window in Chartres blue.

spots.n: Chapelle Notre-Dame de la Médaille Miraculeuse
spots.why: A small chapel on Rue du Bac, one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in France, steps from the Bon Marché.
The classic head-on view of the Eiffel Tower across the Seine, between the two wings of the 1937 Palais de Chaillot.
spots.shot: Both of you with the whole tower behind (sunrise is empty, night has the sparkles).
spots.tips: Come at sunrise for an empty esplanade, or on the hour after dark for the sparkles. Watch for petition and gold-ring scams.
spots.dec: Sunrise is around 8:40 in December, so you don't need to get up early.

spots.why: A two-level bridge with the metro on top and a colonnade walkway underneath (seen in "Inception"), framing the Eiffel Tower.
spots.shot: The colonnade with the tower at the end.

spots.why: A free rooftop with a 360° view: the Opéra right below you, then the Eiffel Tower and Sacré-Cœur.
spots.shot: The Opéra Garnier roof with the Eiffel Tower behind.
spots.dec: Christmas 2026 rooftop ice rink, 24 Nov 2026–3 Jan 2027.

spots.why: A second free department-store rooftop with views of the Opéra, Sacré-Cœur and the Eiffel Tower.
spots.shot: The zinc roofs towards the Eiffel Tower.

spots.nf: Terrasse de l’Institut du monde arabe
spots.why: Jean Nouvel's building with camera-shutter windows and a free 9th-floor terrace looking over Notre-Dame and the Seine.
A hillside park with a sweeping, crowd-free view of the Paris rooftops to the Eiffel Tower. Lovely at sunset.

spots.nf: Rue de l’Université (vue sur la tour Eiffel)
spots.why: The Haussmann street where the Eiffel Tower seems to rise straight out of the buildings: a favourite photo spot.
spots.shot: The tower between the Haussmann façades.
spots.go: Pont de l'Alma (RER C) · École Militaire (M8)

spots.why: The 56th-floor viewpoint, CLOSED from 31 March 2026 for several years of works. For a high view, use the Arc de Triomphe, the Sacré-Cœur dome, the Notre-Dame towers or the department-store rooftops.
The UNESCO-listed riverbanks from the Île Saint-Louis to the Eiffel Tower: bridges, the green-box booksellers (bouquinistes) and the best way to link the sights on foot.
spots.shot: A bridge with the Seine and Notre-Dame behind.
spots.tips: Walk Île Saint-Louis → Notre-Dame → Pont Neuf → Louvre → Pont Alexandre III → Eiffel (about 5 km).

spots.why: The Senate's formal garden: the Medici Fountain, the octagonal pond, green chairs and statues of French queens. The Parisians' favourite park.
spots.tips: Closes at dusk, which is about 16:45–17:00 in December.

spots.why: The royal garden between the Louvre and Concorde, along the axis to the Arc de Triomphe.
spots.shot: The Louvre pyramid seen from the round pond.
spots.dec: "La Magie de Noël" 2026, 14 Nov–3 Jan, 11:00–23:45: Christmas market, ice rink and fairground (Ferris wheel) in the garden.

spots.why: The long lawn running from the Eiffel Tower to the École Militaire: the picnic spot with the tower towering over you.
spots.shot: Lying on the lawn under the tower.
spots.go: École Militaire (M8) · Champ de Mars (RER C)

spots.why: Paris's botanical garden since 1635, with glasshouses (good in winter), a small zoo and the natural-history galleries.
spots.dec: Its winter light festival ran until Jan 2026, but the 2026–27 edition is NOT confirmed (one listing says cancelled). Check before planning.
spots.go: Gare d'Austerlitz (M5, M10, RER C) · Jussieu

spots.why: A dramatic 19th-century park on a former quarry: cliffs, a suspension bridge and the Temple de la Sibylle on top of a rocky island.
spots.shot: The Temple de la Sibylle on its cliff.

spots.why: An elegant English-style park with a colonnade by an oval pond, gold-tipped gates and follies, in the wealthy 8th.
spots.shot: The colonnade reflected in the pond.

spots.why: A 160-year-old amusement garden in the Bois de Boulogne next to the Fondation Louis Vuitton.
spots.dec: Lantern festival "Nuits Indiennes" (India): 27 Nov 2026–21 Feb 2027, 18:00–21:30. About 2,000 lanterns over 6 ha, about €18.

spots.why: Paris's western woods: lakes with rowing boats, the Bagatelle rose garden, the Pré Catelan and the Fondation Louis Vuitton.

spots.nf: Bois de Vincennes et Parc floral
spots.why: Paris's eastern woods, with Lac Daumesnil, the Parc Floral and the château.
The world's first elevated park on an old railway viaduct (1993, before New York's High Line), above the arts-and-crafts arches of the Viaduc des Arts.
spots.shot: The planted walkway between the buildings.
spots.go: Bastille (M1, M5, M8) · Gare de Lyon

spots.why: Elegant 19th-century glasshouses of tropical plants. A warm escape on a cold December day.

spots.nf: Parc André-Citroën et Ballon de Paris
spots.why: A modern riverside park with glasshouses and the tethered Ballon de Paris, which rises 150 m on calm days.
spots.dec: "Patins en Folie" 600 m² outdoor ice rink, 21 Nov 2026–3 Jan 2027, with a light show ("Féeries de Noël") from 4 Dec.

spots.why: A Japanese village garden, English garden and blue forest, with an early-colour photo archive of the world.
Le Nôtre gardens on the hill where a château once stood, with a famous view over Paris from the Lantern terrace.

spots.nf: Balade dans le village de Montmartre
spots.why: The hilltop village of painters (Picasso, Van Gogh, Renoir): cobbled lanes, vineyards, windmills, Sacré-Cœur and the most romantic corners of Paris.
spots.shot: The pink Maison Rose on Rue de l'Abreuvoir.
spots.tips: Route: Abbesses → Mur des Je t'aime → Bateau-Lavoir → Moulin de la Galette → Rue de l'Abreuvoir → vineyard → Place du Tertre → Sacré-Cœur. Go early to beat the crowds.
spots.dec: Montmartre usually has a Christmas market near the Sacré-Cœur (2026 dates not confirmed).

spots.why: Montmartre's painters' square, with portrait artists at their easels. Touristy but iconic.

spots.n: Rue de l'Abreuvoir & La Maison Rose
spots.nf: Rue de l’Abreuvoir et La Maison Rose
spots.why: The prettiest street in Montmartre: the pink café painted by Utrillo, with the Sacré-Cœur dome peeking above the roofs.
spots.shot: The pink house at the corner.

spots.why: A wall of blue tiles with "I love you" written 311 times in 250 languages, in a small square at Abbesses. Made for couples.
spots.shot: Both of you in front of the wall.

spots.why: Medieval lanes and aristocratic mansions turned into Paris's liveliest area: the old Jewish quarter on Rue des Rosiers, boutiques, galleries and the Place des Vosges.
spots.shot: Rue des Rosiers or a hidden mansion courtyard (Hôtel de Sully).
spots.tips: Open on Sundays, when most of Paris is shut. Falafel on Rue des Rosiers.

spots.why: The old student quarter round the Sorbonne: Shakespeare and Company, medieval lanes (Rue de la Huchette, Rue du Chat-qui-Pêche), the Panthéon and Rue Mouffetard.
spots.go: Saint-Michel (M4, RER B, C) · Cluny–La Sorbonne (M10)

spots.why: The Left Bank of Sartre and Hemingway: literary cafés, galleries, fashion boutiques, chocolatiers and the oldest church in Paris.
spots.shot: A table at Café de Flore.
spots.dec: Saint-Germain Christmas market by the church, late Nov–late Dec (2026 dates TBC).

spots.why: A quiet 17th-century island behind Notre-Dame: mansions on the quays, a village high street and Berthillon ice cream.
spots.shot: The back of Notre-Dame from the Pont de la Tournelle.

spots.why: Iron footbridges, locks and plane trees along a 19th-century canal, the bohemian heart of the young Right Bank (seen in "Amélie").
spots.shot: An iron footbridge over the canal.

spots.why: 19th-century glass-roofed shopping arcades with mosaics, old bookshops, toy shops and tea rooms. Perfect on a rainy December day.
spots.shot: The mosaic floor and glass roof of the Galerie Vivienne.
spots.tips: Walk Galerie Vivienne → Passage Choiseul → Passage des Panoramas → Passage Jouffroy → Passage Verdeau.
spots.dec: Charming with their Christmas decorations.

spots.why: One of the oldest streets in Paris: a sloping market street of cheese shops, bakeries and cheap eats down from the Place de la Contrescarpe.
spots.shot: The market stalls at the bottom.

spots.why: A short pedestrian street of pastel-painted houses. Residents ask for quiet, and photo shoots are restricted at some times.
spots.go: Gare de Lyon (M1, M14, RER A, D)

spots.why: A village of cobbled lanes, street art and cheap, lively bars, mostly off the tourist map.
spots.shot: Street art on Rue de la Butte-aux-Cailles.

spots.why: Edith Piaf's neighbourhood: street-art lanes (Rue Dénoyez), Chinese and North African food and the park with the view.
A pedestrian market street of cheese shops, bakeries and cafés near the Eiffel Tower: where to build a picnic.
A food lover's street climbing towards Montmartre, lined with pâtisseries and épiceries.
Old wine warehouses turned into a cobbled street of shops and restaurants, next to the Parc de Bercy.
spots.dec: Usually decorated and lit for Christmas.

spots.why: The coronation cathedral of the French kings (UNESCO) and the champagne capital: cellar tours at Taittinger, Veuve Clicquot, Ruinart or Pommery (book ahead).
spots.shot: The smiling angel on the cathedral façade.
spots.dec: Christmas market 25 Nov–27 Dec 2026 (closed 25 Dec), about 150 chalets at the Hautes Promenades. "Regalia" light show on the cathedral façade at 20:00 on several dates (mostly Fridays and Saturdays) until 2 Jan.

spots.why: The avenue of the great champagne houses (Moët & Chandon, Perrier-Jouët, Pol Roger), with 110 km of cellars beneath it (UNESCO).
spots.go: Épernay (TER/TGV via Reims or direct from Paris-Est, ~1h15)

spots.why: The self-styled 'Capital of Christmas', with France's oldest Christmas market (since 1570), the Gothic cathedral and the half-timbered Petite France quarter. A long day or an overnight.
spots.shot: The giant tree on Place Kléber, or Petite France.
spots.dec: Christkindelsmärik: 27 Nov–24 Dec 2026, daily 11:30–21:00 (closes 18:00 on 24 Dec). Colmar's markets open from 23 Nov.

spots.why: France's biggest light festival: four nights of light installations across Lyon's old town, free.
spots.shot: The light show on Place des Terreaux or Fourvière.
spots.dec: 5–8 Dec 2026 (Sat–Tue), about 18:00–midnight. Huge crowds; book the train and any hotel early.
spots.go: Lyon Part-Dieu (TGV from Gare de Lyon, ~2h)

spots.why: A half-timbered Normandy city: the cathedral Monet painted 30 times, the Gros-Horloge clock and the square where Joan of Arc was burned.
spots.dec: Christmas market by the cathedral (check 2026 dates).

spots.why: A UNESCO-listed medieval fair town with ramparts, the Tour César and underground passages. Quieter in winter, when some shows stop.
spots.go: Provins (Transilien P from Gare de l'Est, ~1h20)

spots.why: A small, perfectly kept medieval town with a Gothic cathedral, 10 minutes from Chantilly. Combine the two in one day.
The abbey on a tidal island (UNESCO), one of the most famous sights in France. About 4 hours each way, so it is best with an overnight.
spots.shot: The Mount from the footbridge across the bay.
spots.go: TGV to Rennes (~1h30) + bus (~1h10), or a coach tour

spots.why: The village where Van Gogh spent his last 70 days and painted about 80 canvases. He and Theo are buried here. Many sites close in winter.

spots.n: Giverny – Monet's house & gardens (closed in December)
spots.nf: Giverny – maison et jardins de Monet (fermés en décembre)
spots.why: Monet's house and water-lily garden with its Japanese bridge. CLOSED in winter: the 2026 season ran 1 April–1 November, so it cannot be visited in December. Keep it for a spring trip.
spots.shot: The Japanese bridge over the water lilies.

spots.why: A Belle Époque station buffet (1901) that is a listed historic monument: gilded ceilings, 41 paintings and classic French food. Even a drink at the bar is worth it.
spots.tips: Restaurant 11:15–14:30 and 19:00–22:30; the bar lounge is open 7:30–22:30.
spots.go: Gare de Lyon (M1, M14, RER A, D)

spots.why: A workers' canteen since 1896 serving cheap French classics (snails, steak-frites) in a listed dining hall, with waiters writing the bill on the paper tablecloth.
spots.tips: Expect a queue; go early or late.

spots.why: The most beautiful Art Nouveau dining room in Paris (Édith Piaf's table is still there), now a cheap bouillon.
A modern bouillon with very cheap French classics, handy before or after the Moulin Rouge.
Only one dish, steak-frites with a secret green sauce, served twice. No bookings, so expect a queue.
Paris's oldest café-restaurant (1686), where Voltaire, Rousseau and Benjamin Franklin met. Napoleon's hat is on display.
A bistro unchanged since 1845 (Hemingway ate here, and so did Owen in 'Midnight in Paris'), with cheap traditional dishes.
An Alsatian brasserie of writers and politicians since 1880, with Art Nouveau ceramics, choucroute and sausages.
The great Art Deco brasserie of Montparnasse (1927), with painted pillars, seafood platters and lamb curry.
A Belle Époque brasserie (1864) under a stained-glass dome: oysters, choucroute and seafood platters.
spots.dec: Oysters are at their best in December.

spots.why: A gilded restaurant under the Palais-Royal arcades since 1784, where Napoleon and Joséphine dined. The plaques name the famous guests. Special occasion.
Fine dining on the Eiffel Tower's 2nd floor (Frédéric Anton). A once-in-a-lifetime special occasion; book months ahead.
A brasserie on the Eiffel Tower's 1st floor (Thierry Marx), easier and cheaper than the Jules Verne.

spots.nf: Les Ombres (toit du musée du quai Branly)
spots.why: A glass-roofed restaurant on top of the quai Branly museum, with the Eiffel Tower filling the window.
spots.shot: The tower through the glass roof at night.

spots.why: Paris's most famous falafel pitta, in the old Jewish quarter of the Marais. Fast-moving queue.
spots.shot: The pitta in hand on Rue des Rosiers.
spots.tips: Closed from Friday evening to Saturday (Shabbat).

spots.why: Some of the best Breton galettes and crêpes in Paris, with organic buckwheat and craft cider.
A classic of the Breton crêpe street by the Montparnasse station, with lace-crisp galettes.
A four-floor Italian trattoria from the Big Mamma group, with a glasshouse top floor. Wildly popular on Instagram.
The textbook Paris bistro: zinc bar, chalkboard menu, steak au poivre and Paris-Brest.
One of Paris's most sought-after neo-bistros (Michelin-starred), with a relaxed seasonal tasting menu. Bookings open about 3 weeks ahead and go in minutes.
A loud, generous Basque bistro near the Eiffel Tower. The rice pudding is famous.
Yves Camdeborde's Saint-Germain bistro on the Carrefour de l'Odéon.
Paris's archetypal bistro since 1912, now run by Alain Ducasse: lacquered wood, red velvet and classics such as cassoulet and profiteroles.
A Provençal bistro behind the Place des Vosges, with 80 pastis and an all-you-can-eat bowl of chocolate mousse.
The old Les Halles market brasserie, open late, with onion soup, oysters and pig's trotters.
spots.go: Les Halles (M4, RER A, B, D)

spots.why: A tiny Montmartre cave serving fondue, with wine in baby bottles and benches you climb over the table to reach. A fun winter evening.
A corner café-restaurant once frequented by Montmartre's painters, on the most photographed crossroads of the hill.
Christian Le Squer's three-Michelin-star table (2026 Guide) in the George V, known for its flower arrangements.
Arnaud Donckele's three-star restaurant (2026 Guide) in the Samaritaine building, overlooking the Seine.
Alain Passard's vegetable-led three-star restaurant (2026 Guide) next to the Musée Rodin.

ph.by: Kent Wang from London, United Kingdom

spots.why: Frédéric Anton's three-star restaurant (2026 Guide) in a Napoleon III pavilion in the Bois de Boulogne.
Yannick Alléno's restaurant inside the Dior flagship, which won its first Michelin star in the 2026 Guide. A natural pairing with the Dior Christmas façade.
The Art Deco café where Sartre and de Beauvoir wrote. Pricey, but a hot chocolate on the heated terrace is a rite of passage.
spots.shot: Hot chocolate at a terrace table.

spots.why: Flore's rival next door (Hemingway, Picasso), facing the oldest church in Paris. Known for its old-fashioned hot chocolate.

ph.by: Cheng-en Cheng from Taichung City, Taiwan

spots.why: A Belle Époque tea room (1903) famous for its thick 'L'Africain' hot chocolate and Mont-Blanc pastry. A December essential.
spots.shot: The hot chocolate jug and a Mont-Blanc.
spots.tips: The queue moves faster mid-afternoon on weekdays, or buy to take away at the shop counter.
spots.dec: Hot-chocolate season; combine with the Tuileries Christmas market across the street.

spots.why: A 1927 pâtisserie on the Place du Trocadéro, with macarons, hot chocolate and the Eiffel Tower round the corner. A second branch is on the Place des Vosges.
The house that made the double-decker macaron famous (founded 1862 on Rue Royale), with a gilded tea room on the Champs-Élysées.
The 'Picasso of pastry': the Ispahan (rose, lychee, raspberry) and some of the best macarons in Paris.
spots.dec: Look for his Christmas bûches.

spots.why: The pastry star of Instagram: trompe-l'œil fruits and some of the most photographed viennoiseries in Paris. Long queues.
Paris's oldest pâtisserie (1730), founded by Louis XV's queen's pastry chef. It invented the baba au rhum.
A bakery in a listed 1889 shop near the Canal Saint-Martin, famous for its pistachio-chocolate "escargot" pastry.

spots.n: Boulangerie du Sentier (best croissant, Grand Paris 2026)
spots.nf: Boulangerie du Sentier (meilleur croissant du Grand Paris 2026)
spots.why: Ranked no. 1 for butter croissant in the 2026 Grand Paris competition (Fête du Pain, 12 May 2026).

spots.n: Le Fournil Didot (best baguette of Paris 2026)
spots.nf: Le Fournil Didot (meilleure baguette de Paris 2026)
spots.why: Winner of the city's 2026 Grand Prix for the best baguette (Sithamparappillai Jegatheepan). It supplies the Élysée Palace for a year.

spots.n: L'Épi du Roi (best croissant in France 2026)
spots.nf: L’Épi du Roi (meilleur croissant de France 2026)
spots.why: Dylan Delmaire's bakery in Versailles, crowned best butter croissant in France in June 2026. An easy stop on the Versailles day.
The famous wood-fired sourdough loaf, baked here since 1932, and buttery "punitions" biscuits.
Paris's most famous ice cream since 1954 (try salted caramel or wild strawberry), on the Île Saint-Louis.
A chocolatier and caramel maker in a Marais workshop. Come for the mango-passion caramels and a cup of hot chocolate.
Paris's oldest chocolate and sweet shop (1761), with its original shopfront.
spots.dec: Christmas chocolates and marrons glacés.

spots.why: A tea house since 1854: hundreds of teas in black tins and a colonial-style tea room.

spots.nf: Salon de thé de la Grande Mosquée
spots.why: Mint tea and North African pastries under the fig trees of the mosque courtyard, cheap and charming.

ph.by: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra (Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France)

spots.why: The café next to the legendary bookshop, facing Notre-Dame.
spots.shot: The shop front with Notre-Dame behind.

spots.why: The original cabaret revue: feathers, rhinestones and the French cancan, with dinner or champagne options.
spots.shot: The windmill on your way in.

spots.why: The stylish, arty cabaret of light and nude dance on Avenue George V.
A tiny Montmartre cabaret of old French songs, in the same cottage since the 1860s, where Picasso drank.

ph.by: David McSpadden from Daly City, United States

spots.why: A swing-jazz cellar in a medieval vault since 1946, where people still dance (it appears in 'La La Land').
Rue des Lombards' leading jazz club, with intimate seated concerts.
Two jazz clubs in one building, acoustic upstairs and electric downstairs.

spots.n: Ritz Paris bars (Ritz Bar & Bar Hemingway)
spots.nf: Bars du Ritz Paris (Ritz Bar et Bar Hemingway)
spots.why: The Ritz's bars: the tiny wood-panelled Bar Hemingway, named after its most famous drinker, and the Ritz Bar (about 17:30–23:30). Go after the Place Vendôme Christmas trees.
spots.dec: The Ritz is dressed for Christmas (teddy-bear theme in 2025; the 2026 décor is not yet published).

spots.why: An American bar since 1911 that claims to have invented the Bloody Mary.
spots.shot: A Bloody Mary at the bar.

spots.why: A Marais cocktail bar regularly ranked among the World's 50 Best Bars, behind a small red door.
A speakeasy behind the white door at the back of a tiny taqueria.
A wine bar with wine from the barrel by the Aligre market. On winter weekends an oyster seller sets up on the pavement outside.
spots.dec: December is the heart of oyster season.

spots.why: A traditional circus in its own 1852 building. The 2026–27 show "Volte" (trapeze, diabolo, comedy and breakdance) runs until 7 Mar 2027.
Jean Nouvel's concert hall, one of the best in Europe for sound, in the Parc de la Villette.
spots.shot: The aluminium birds on the façade.

spots.nf: Spectacles à l’Opéra Bastille et au Palais Garnier
spots.why: The Paris Opera's ballet and opera season (December 2026 programme not checked here: see operadeparis.fr). Last-minute cheap tickets are sometimes released.
The Belle Époque department store under a stained-glass dome (1912), with a free rooftop and a gourmet food hall. In December it is a sight in itself.
spots.shot: The giant tree under the dome.
spots.dec: Christmas 2026, "Au cœur de Noël" by Jean-Charles de Castelbajac: the tree under the dome and the windows (a character called Armand, angels, a fashion parade), 12 Nov 2026–3 Jan 2027. Free. The tree has drawn criticism online, so judge for yourselves. Rooftop ice rink 24 Nov–3 Jan.

spots.why: The other great department store, with an Art Nouveau dome and a rooftop. Its animated Christmas windows are a Paris tradition.
spots.dec: Windows 2026, "Un Noël bien tricoté": cats, mice and balls of yarn, with 160 hand-made characters, visible until 3 Jan 2027. The inauguration was postponed as a precaution during demonstrations.

spots.why: The world's first department store (1852), with an Eiffel-era iron structure and the most refined selection in Paris.
spots.dec: "Village Noël" 2026, a mountain village of chalets and fir trees, 24 Oct–31 Dec.

spots.why: Le Bon Marché's huge luxury food hall, the best place for edible gifts (mustards, chocolate, foie gras, wine).
spots.dec: Christmas foods and bûches.

spots.why: A department store by the Pont Neuf, reopened in 2021 after a 16-year restoration: an Art Nouveau peacock fresco under a glass roof.
spots.shot: The peacock fresco and glass roof.
spots.dec: Reported "Balade de Noël" market of decorations under the glass roof, 4 Nov 2026–5 Jan 2027 (only one source; check).

spots.why: The haute-couture avenue (Dior, Chanel, Valentino, Prada), with the Plaza Athénée's red awnings.
spots.shot: The Dior façade at 30 Montaigne lit for Christmas.
spots.dec: Avenue lights switched on Thu 19 Nov 2026. The Dior façade and animated windows are inspired by the animated film "Christian Dior's Night in Color" (dir. Sylvain Chomet), from ~14 Nov. The Plaza Athénée has an ice rink and raclette chalet in its courtyard, 26 Nov 2026–31 Jan 2027.

spots.why: Luxury street of Hermès's flagship at no. 24 (famous windows), Chanel nearby, the Élysée Palace and the palace hotels.
spots.dec: Christmas lights and dressed windows from late November.

spots.why: Guerlain's perfume flagship since 1914, with a gilded staircase.
The most famous English-language bookshop in the world, opposite Notre-Dame (opened 1951, heir to Sylvia Beach's original).
spots.tips: No photos inside.

spots.why: The green booksellers' boxes along the quays since the 16th century, with old prints, postcards and books.
spots.shot: A green box with Notre-Dame behind.

spots.why: The world's largest antiques and flea market: 1,700 dealers in a maze of covered markets (Vernaison, Paul Bert Serpette).
spots.tips: Open Saturday to Monday. Ignore the counterfeit stalls by the metro and go straight to the antiques markets.

spots.why: Paris's oldest covered market (1628), with food stalls (Moroccan, Japanese, Italian, crêpes) and communal tables.
A lively, cheap food market with a covered hall (Beauvau) and a small flea market.
One of the biggest open-air markets in Paris, on Thursday and Sunday mornings.
A cabinet of curiosities since 1831: taxidermy lions, butterflies and old school charts (it appears in 'Midnight in Paris').
A professional cookware shop since 1820, packed with copper pans, where Julia Child shopped.
spots.go: Les Halles (M4, RER A, B, D)

spots.why: A design concept store with the little red car in the courtyard and a used-book café.
spots.shot: The red Fiat in the courtyard.

spots.why: A wine shop and bar from 1880 at the entrance to the Galerie Vivienne, good for French wine to take home.
A luxury outlet village of about 110 boutiques (Gucci, Prada, Saint Laurent, Sandro...) at 30%+ off, next to Disneyland.
spots.tips: Shopping Express coach from Bercy daily at 9:00 (back at 14:30 or 18:45), or the RER A. Tax-free for non-EU residents. Combine with Disneyland.
spots.dec: Decorated for Christmas. Closed 25 Dec.
spots.go: Val d'Europe (RER A, ~40 min) + 10 min walk · Shopping Express coach

spots.why: An hour on the Seine past Notre-Dame, the Louvre, the Orsay and the Eiffel Tower. The easiest first-day overview and lovely after dark. Several companies: Bateaux-Mouches (from Pont de l'Alma), Vedettes du Pont Neuf, Bateaux Parisiens.
spots.shot: The Eiffel Tower sparkling from the boat.
spots.tips: Take an after-dark cruise for the lit monuments; dinner cruises are for special occasions.
spots.dec: After dark from about 17:00, so evening cruises are easy to fit in.

spots.why: Europe's most visited theme park: two parks (Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World, with the new World of Frozen).
spots.shot: Sleeping Beauty Castle lit for Christmas.
spots.dec: "Disney Enchanted Christmas", 7 Nov 2026–6 Jan 2027, now extended to World of Frozen. Santa until 25 Dec. New Year's Eve celebrations included in the ticket.

spots.why: The 90-second ride up to the Sacré-Cœur, for the price of a metro ticket, skipping 222 steps.

spots.nf: Cours de pâtisserie ou de macarons
spots.why: Learn to make croissants or macarons in English. Several schools (La Cuisine Paris, Le Foodist, Galeries Lafayette). Good on a rainy day and as a couple.
A guided tasting of French wines with cheese (O Chateau and others). A good crash course before the bistros.
spots.go: Les Halles (M4, RER A, B, D)

spots.why: Two-Michelin-star French restaurant on the 6th floor of The Peninsula, with a terrace looking at the Eiffel Tower and Sacré-Cœur. Chic, elegant dress code.
spots.shot: Your table with the Eiffel Tower behind.
spots.tips: Lunch 12:00–14:00, dinner 19:00–22:00, every day.

spots.why: Big Mamma's most upmarket Italian (Riviera style, opulent room), a few steps from the Musée d'Orsay. Very popular.
spots.tips: Lunch about 12:00–14:30, dinner 19:00–22:30 (check).

spots.why: Dior's spa in the basement of the Cheval Blanc palace (the old Samaritaine building): six treatment suites in white onyx, hammam, sauna and a snow shower.
spots.tips: Book treatments well ahead; ask about access to the pool with a treatment.

spots.why: The 1630 grotto fountain built for Marie de' Medici, with a long pond under the plane trees: the most romantic corner of the Luxembourg.
spots.shot: The two of you at the end of the pond.
spots.tips: Inside the Luxembourg, so it closes with the garden (about 16:45 in December).

spots.why: A short stepped street with lamp posts, dropping from the Place du Tertre: one of the most picturesque corners of Montmartre.
spots.shot: Looking down the steps with the lamp posts.

spots.why: The historic National Library, reopened in 2022: the Salle Ovale reading room under its glass dome (free) and a museum of the library's treasures.
spots.shot: The Salle Ovale from the entrance.
spots.tips: Salle Ovale is free; the museum is €15 (from 1 Sep 2026). Closed on Mondays. Next to the Galerie Vivienne.

spots.why: A Belle Époque brasserie on the Grands Boulevards next to the Opéra, open late: seafood platters and onion soup after the department stores.
The chic Italian restaurant of the Musée des Arts Décoratifs, with a big terrace facing the Louvre and the Tuileries.
spots.shot: The terrace with the Louvre behind.
spots.tips: Hours differ by source (roughly 12:00–15:00 and 19:00–23:00); book by phone.

spots.why: A 1930s-style seafood restaurant designed by Joseph Dirand at the Cité de l'Architecture, with a terrace facing the Eiffel Tower.
spots.shot: The tower from the terrace at night.
spots.tips: Dinner daily (last order ~23:00), lunch at weekends (check). Book by phone.

spots.why: The Mandarin Oriental's all-day restaurant around its garden courtyard; chef Nina Haradji since September 2025 (after Thierry Marx).
A small arthouse cinema off the Champs-Élysées showing films in their original language.

spots.nf: Grand Brunch du dimanche au Ritz Paris
spots.why: The Ritz's Sunday brunch buffet under the glass roof, 11:45–14:30. Festive brunches (Easter, 14 July) were €295 per person in 2026.
spots.shot: The buffet under the glass roof.
spots.tips: Sundays only. In your dates: 20 and 27 Dec. Book well ahead.

spots.why: A literary hotel in the upper Marais decorated by Jacques Garcia in Belle Époque style; the velvet bar with Venetian mirrors pours 17:00–01:00.
Paris Society's restaurant inside the Palais Garnier (the opera house's east rotunda): a theatrical room, smart dress code.
spots.shot: The dining room under the opera house.
spots.tips: Pair it with an Opéra visit or the Galeries Lafayette windows.

spots.n: Abbaye des Vaux de Cernay (hotel & spa)
spots.nf: Abbaye des Vaux de Cernay (hôtel et spa)
spots.why: A 12th-century Cistercian abbey in the Chevreuse valley woods, turned into a 104-room hotel by Paris Society in late 2023, with a spa and the abbey ruins in the park.
spots.shot: The abbey ruins by the pond.
spots.tips: A natural night after a Versailles day (25 min away). Prices vary a lot by date.
spots.go: By car: ~50 min from central Paris, ~25 min from Versailles

spots.why: Paris Society's grand restaurant in the Hôtel Salomon de Rothschild, a homage to Baroness Adèle de Rothschild, near the Étoile.
A hidden 18th-century chapel of the Spiritans, behind a façade by Chalgrin (the Arc de Triomphe's architect), with a surprisingly rich interior.
spots.tips: Opening times are irregular; check before going.

spots.why: An explorers-themed café-brasserie in the arcades of the Hôtel de la Marine, open 8:00–23:00 every day (breakfast until 11:00).
A Franco-Slavic restaurant (Paris Society) in a 1910 Art Nouveau mansion near Place Victor-Hugo; bar until 02:00.
The glass-roofed restaurant inside RH Paris, the American design gallery-store on the Champs-Élysées. Weekend brunch.
spots.shot: Under the glass roof with the chandeliers.
spots.tips: About 12:00–22:00 (23:00 Fri–Sat); hours differ by source.

spots.nf: Le Petit RH (toit de RH Paris)
spots.why: The small rooftop restaurant of RH Paris (caviar, champagne) above the Champs-Élysées.
spots.shot: The rooftop view over the avenue.
spots.tips: Daily from noon to 21:30 (22:00 Fri–Sat).

spots.why: A festive Italian restaurant with a piano-bar, live music or DJ sets late into the night.
spots.tips: Open until about 01:00–02:00; hours differ by source.

spots.nf: Francette (péniche au pied de la tour Eiffel)
spots.why: A barge at the foot of the Eiffel Tower with a restaurant, bistro, rooftop and an underwater wine cellar. Reviews say the view beats the food.

ph.by: Steven Penton from Bakers Beach, Tasmania Australia

spots.nf: Café Dior et Le Jardin (30 Montaigne)
spots.why: The café and the garden tea room (lunch, afternoon tea) inside Dior's 30 Montaigne flagship, by Yannick Alléno, next to the Monsieur Dior restaurant.
spots.dec: Combine with the Dior Christmas façade and windows at 30 Montaigne.

spots.why: Simone Zanoni's convivial Mediterranean restaurant in the George V; its Michelin star was kept in 2026. Famous flower arrangements in the lobby.

spots.nf: Avenue de Camoëns (vue sur la tour Eiffel)
spots.why: A quiet Haussmann avenue ending in a balustrade and steps with a full, crowd-free view of the Eiffel Tower.
spots.shot: The two of you at the balustrade with the tower behind.

spots.why: The white chalk cliffs, arches and needle of the Normandy coast painted by Monet. A long day by car; in Normandy, not Brittany.
spots.shot: The Porte d'Aval arch and the needle from the cliff path.
spots.tips: Paid parking all year 9:00–19:00; park at the edge of town. Check low tide before going down to the beach and keep away from the cliff foot (falling rock).
spots.go: By car: ~2h45 from central Paris (~210 km)

spots.why: The small Normandy port on the Seine estuary: tall slate-fronted houses round the Vieux Bassin, and Sainte-Catherine, the largest wooden church in France. Boudin and Monet painted here.
spots.shot: The Vieux Bassin houses reflected in the water.
spots.tips: Park in the paid car parks by the harbour and walk; the old town is small. Pairs well with Étretat and Deauville in one day.
spots.dec: Christmas market round the old harbour, about 18 Dec 2026–3 Jan 2027 (check the dates).
spots.go: By car: ~2h15 from central Paris (~200 km); 50 min from Étretat over the Pont de Normandie (toll)

spots.why: The chic seaside resort of the Normandy coast: the 1920s boardwalk with beach cabins named after film stars, Belle Époque villas, the casino and the palace hotels.
spots.shot: The beach cabins on Les Planches at sunset.
spots.tips: Best at the end of the day: walk Les Planches at sunset, then the shopping streets by the casino. Paid parking near the seafront.
spots.go: By car: ~2h from central Paris (~200 km, A13); 20 min from Honfleur

spots.why: A vertical wind tunnel in the Vill'Up mall at the Cité des Sciences: a first flight takes about 1h30 with the briefing.

spots.n: Tennis at the Jardin du Luxembourg
spots.why: Outdoor courts in the Luxembourg garden, run by the Senate. A fun Parisian thing to do, weather permitting in December.
spots.shot: On court with the garden around.
spots.tips: Check how to book and the winter hours.

spots.why: The French President's palace on the Faubourg Saint-Honoré. You can only see the gate from the street; it opens inside on the Heritage Days in September.

ph.by: U.S. Department of State from United States

spots.why: Europe's biggest cinema hall (about 2,700 seats) under an Art Deco starry sky. Its Christmas tradition is the 'Féerie des Eaux' water show before a Disney film.
spots.shot: The Art Deco tower sign at night.
spots.dec: "La Féerie des Eaux" + Disney's "Billie, à la croisée des mondes" (in French): 25 Nov 2026–3 Jan 2027, sessions 10:30, 13:15 and 16:00, ~2h15, ~€16–18.

spots.why: A huge pedestrian square round the statue of Marianne, a gathering point between the Marais and the Canal Saint-Martin.

spots.n: Château d'Écouen – Musée national de la Renaissance
spots.why: A Renaissance château on a hill, home to the national museum of the Renaissance (the 75 m "David and Bathsheba" tapestry). Quiet, and rarely crowded.
spots.go: By car: ~35 min from central Paris

spots.why: The largest Cistercian abbey in Île-de-France, founded by Saint Louis in 1228, with gardens and concerts. Monthly brunch on the last Sunday.
spots.go: By car: ~45 min from central Paris

spots.why: France's second theme park, built on the Astérix comics, with some of Europe's best roller coasters. Closed in winter except for the Christmas season.

trips.sub_fr: 16–30 déc. 2026 : vitrines et illuminations, grands musées les jours d’ouverture, Versailles, châteaux de nuit et un jour de Noël sur la côte normande. Un parking par groupe de lieux.

2026-12-16.note: Allow 40 min to an hour by car from the suburbs. Crit'Air sticker needed in Paris; use the car parks the app shows, as heavy cars pay a higher street rate. Galeries Lafayette: tree under the dome and the rooftop, then the Printemps windows opposite, best after dark (~17:00). Opéra Garnier lit up; dinner at Le Grand Café Capucines or BeauCoco.

2026-12-17.note: Louvre at opening (timed slot), pick 3–4 wings (closed Tuesdays, so Thursday is right). Lunch: Loulou or Café Lapérouse. Tuileries fair → Concorde → Hôtel de la Marine. Dusk: Place Vendôme trees → Ritz Bar / Bar Hemingway → Champs-Élysées lights. You may drive into the 1st–4th to reach a car park, not to cross it.

2026-12-18.t: Île de la Cité & Left Bank
2026-12-18.note: Notre-Dame early (free slot) and towers → Sainte-Chapelle in morning light → Conciergerie. Lunch: Polidor. Shakespeare and Company → Panthéon → chapel at 30 rue Lhomond → Luxembourg and Fontaine Médicis before ~16:45 (gates shut at dusk). Evening: Café de Flore, or the 18:00 Vivaldi concert at the Sainte-Chapelle. Calm weekday before the school holidays.

2026-12-19.note: Saturday: Montmartre early (Abbesses → Mur des Je t'aime → Rue de l'Abreuvoir → Rue du Calvaire → Place du Tertre → Sacré-Cœur, dome if clear). Streets are steep and narrow: park at Anvers or Blanche. Lunch: Le Consulat or Pink Mamma. Afternoon: Galerie Vivienne and the passages → BnF Richelieu → Bourse de Commerce. Evening: Moulin Rouge (21:00) or Siena.

2026-12-20.note: Ritz Sunday Grand Brunch (11:45, book well ahead). Then the Marais, open on Sundays: Place des Vosges → Musée Carnavalet (free) or Picasso → Rue des Rosiers. Evening: Maison Proust bar → dinner at Chez Janou. Park near Vendôme for the brunch, then move the car to a Marais car park (10 min).

2026-12-21.note: About 35 min by car. Château de Chantilly and the Musée Condé; the Great Stables' Christmas show; or Senlis old town. Monday: many Paris museums are closed, Chantilly is open (it closes on Tuesdays).

2026-12-22.t: Versailles (+ optional night at the abbey)
2026-12-22.note: About 40 min by car. Palace at opening, then the Trianon; croissant from L'Épi du Roi. Gardens free in winter; evening show-visit Le Parcours du Roi (18:00–20:05 departures). Option: a night at the Abbaye des Vaux de Cernay (25 min). Tuesday is the best day: closed Mondays, packed at weekends.

2026-12-23.note: Orsay at opening (5th floor first, closed Mondays); lunch at Gloria Osteria. Rodin or the Invalides → Rue de l'Université and Avenue de Camoëns photos → Eiffel Tower ~15:30 (summit in daylight, book weeks ahead). Trocadéro for the 18:00 or 19:00 sparkle → Girafe or Francette → night Seine cruise. Two car parks: Orsay/Invalides, then the tower.

2026-12-24.note: Arc de Triomphe roof → down the Champs-Élysées; lunch at Le Jardin RH or Le Petit RH. Avenue Montaigne (Dior, Café Dior), Faubourg Saint-Honoré windows, the Élysée gate. Shops close early. Home for the réveillon; optional Notre-Dame midnight mass (free, arrive early).

2026-12-25.note: Decide the day before, with the weather. 1) Recommended: coast loop Étretat cliffs → Honfleur (Christmas market 18 Dec–3 Jan) → Deauville seafront; about 2h–2h45 each way, daylight ~08:55–17:03, so leave by 7:30. 2) Mont-Saint-Michel: about 4h each way and the abbey is closed today; only worth it as an overnight (big tides 25–27 Dec). 3) Stay with family; Notre-Dame masses 8:30, 10:00, 11:30.

2026-12-26.t: Shopping day: La Vallée Village (+ Disneyland evening)
2026-12-26.note: About 1h by car to La Vallée Village at opening (the post-Christmas Saturday is busy). Optionally Disneyland next door for the Christmas parade and the night show.

2026-12-27.t: Sunday by car: Fontainebleau + Vaux-le-Vicomte by night
2026-12-27.note: About 1h15 to Fontainebleau palace (closed Tuesdays); lunch in town. Then 25 min to Vaux-le-Vicomte's Grand Noël (book online) and stay for the lights after dark; about 1h15 home.

2026-12-28.note: A short day north of Paris (Étretat moved to the 25th): Auvers-sur-Oise (~15 min), Abbaye de Royaumont, Château d'Écouen. If the coast did not happen on the 25th, do Étretat today: about 2h45, check the low tide, back before dark (~17:00).

2026-12-29.note: Petit Palais (free) → Pont Alexandre III; lunch at Le George or Baronne. Jacquemart-André (tea room) → Madeleine → Grand Palais skating (14:00–19:00, online only). Pont Alexandre III lit up at night → L'Oiseau Blanc or Maison Revka.

2026-12-30.note: Dior Spa Cheval Blanc → La Samaritaine; lunch at Camélia. Fondation Louis Vuitton (open Wednesdays), the Grand Rex, or iFLY. Jardin d'Acclimatation lanterns (18:00–21:30), next to the Fondation. Spare time for anything missed or rained out.
